newsitem.title: USA: Ranson Capital unveils first Oklahoma muni fund.
newsitem.headline: Ranson Capital unveils first Oklahoma muni fund.

text.p: Ranson Capital Corp, a subsidiary of ND Holdings, opened the first tax-exempt municipal bond fund specializing in Oklahoma debt, the company said in a release.

"Even though single-state municipal bond funds have been available in most of the other states for years, the Oklahoma Municipal Fund provides Oklahoma residents with their first opportunity to invest in a mutual fund that produces a flow of income exempt from both state and federal income taxes," Robert Walstad, the fund's president, said in the release.

Walstad said the absence of funds was due in part to the limited amount of state and local government debt issued in Oklahoma compared to other states. Given that situation, the Oklahoma Municipal Fund may invest up to 30 percent of its assets in securities that are not tax-exempt from Oklahoma income taxes, although managers intend to invest as close as possible to 100 percent in Oklahoma debt.
Alex Meitzner will serve as the fund's portfolio manager.

"We have been involved with the municipal bond market in this region since 1984," Meitzner said. "Over that time we have built strong relationships with local, regional and national municipal bond dealers as well as bond underwriters. These relationships should serve us well in obtaining double tax-exempt Oklahoma bonds for the fund."

Ranson Capital also manages tax-exempt municipal bond funds for Kansas and Nebraska residents. In addition, parent company ND Holdings Inc sponsors similar funds for residents of North Dakota, South Dakota and Montana.
